answer: Give each identity a marble stake locked on a public terrace: the higher the terrace, the more voting weight, but climbing requires a fresh cipher-bound proof of distinct work each epoch, a signed computation no two identities can share. Clones pile onto the lowest terrace because forging distinct proofs per clone costs real compute, while one honest agent climbs cheaply on its own work. A sybil farmer must pay the full climb for every fake.
